definitions.explanation: The chemical process in which microorganisms such as yeast or bacteria break down substances, typically producing alcohol, acids, or gases. Fundamental to many Japanese foods and beverages including sake, miso, soy sauce, and pickles.

examples.japanese: ⟦{味噌|みそ}→味噌：01037_miso⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{大豆|だいず}→大豆：10536_daizu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{発酵|はっこう}⟦させて→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{作|つく}る→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
examples.english: Miso is made by fermenting soybeans.

examples.japanese: {発酵|はっこう}⟦{食品|しょくひん}→食品：03247_shokuhin⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{健康|けんこう}→健康：02706_kenkou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{良|よ}い→良い：02350_yoi⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}われている→言う：00515_iu⟧。

notes:
USAGE:
Functions as a ⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ verb: {発酵|はっこう}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to ferment, intransitive) and {発酵|はっこう}⟦させる→する：00392_suru⟧ (to ferment, transitive/causative). Japan has a particularly rich tradition of fermented foods, and {発酵|はっこう} frequently appears in discussions of food culture.

JAPANESE FERMENTED FOODS:
- ⟦{味噌|みそ}→味噌：01037_miso⟧: miso (fermented soybean paste)
- ⟦{醤油|しょうゆ}→醤油：01056_shouyu⟧: soy sauce
- ⟦{納豆|なっとう}→納豆：04930_nattou⟧: natto (fermented soybeans)
- ⟦{漬物|つけもの}→漬物：04938_tsukemono⟧: pickles (many types use fermentation)
- ⟦{日本酒|にほんしゅ}→日本酒：12954_nihonshu⟧: sake

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {発酵|はっこう}⟦{食品|しょくひん}→食品：03247_shokuhin⟧: fermented food
- {発酵|はっこう}⟦させる→する：00392_suru⟧: to ferment (something)
